resource-based.md: "Attribute evaluation occurs before data binding and before execution of any method that loads a resource. Declarative authorization with an [Authorize] attribute doesn't suffice for resource-based authorization." authentication/index.md: authentication "is used by authentication middleware". But introduction.md: "ASP.NET Core authorization provides a simple declarative role and a rich policy-based model" - authorization is not always per resource; [Authorize] itself is authorization that needs no data.
claim_verdicts.suggested_text: In ASP.NET Core, authentication runs in middleware on every request. Some authorization, like [Authorize], needs only the caller; an ownership check (does this caller own this order?) needs the resource, so it is made per endpoint after the resource is loaded.

claim_verdicts.evidence: Follows from the code in claim 4: the query is Where(o => o.CustomerId == customerId) with customerId taken from the caller's sub, so rows with another customer_id are never read. Confirmed live (claim 5): order 3 (customer_id 2) absent from customer 1's list.

issues.quote: The previous lesson was entirely about this question, and a request that fails it gets `401`.
issues.text: Unlisted claim, and false for the endpoint this lesson is about. A request that fails authentication gets 401 only from an endpoint marked [Authorize]. Live at stage-1: GET /api/v1/orders/3 with 'Authorization: Bearer abc.def.ghi' -> 200; with no header -> 200; GET /api/v1/orders with the same bad token -> 401. Section 5 itself says Get 'does not even require a caller', so the two sections contradict each other.
issues.fix: Replace with: "The previous lesson was entirely about this question: on an endpoint marked `[Authorize]`, a request that fails it gets `401`." Add a claim (kind behavior, source: live curl with a malformed token to /orders/3 -> 200 and /orders -> 401).

issues.quote: Authorization cannot be done once: whether customer 1 may read order 3 depends on order 3
issues.text: Overgeneralised, repeated in section 6 ("authorization checks the caller against the thing being asked for, so it needs the data and differs per endpoint") and summary line 3 ("Authorization depends on the data"). ASP.NET Core docs: authorization includes a declarative role/policy model; [Authorize], which this lesson uses, is authorization evaluated before any data is loaded. Only resource-based checks such as ownership need the data (resource-based.md). Section 3 already qualifies correctly ("can differ per endpoint and per resource"); these sentences drop the qualifier. See claim 7.
issues.fix: Section 4: "An ownership check cannot be done once: whether customer 1 may read order 3 depends on order 3...". Section 6: "...an ownership check compares the caller with the thing being asked for, so it needs the data...". Summary 3: "An ownership check depends on the data, so each endpoint that touches someone's data has to make it for that data." Replace claim 7 text with its suggested_text.

issues.quote: Order 3 does exist, and the lesson frames the right answer as `403`: the refusal is about ownership, not about a missing resource.
issues.text: Key a is correct given the lesson text, but option c is not wrong in general: RFC 9110 15.5.4 says "An origin server that wishes to 'hide' the current existence of a forbidden target resource MAY instead respond with a status code of 404 (Not Found)." The explanation for c implies 404 would be incorrect.
issues.fix: Explanation c (en): "Order 3 does exist. An API may choose 404 to hide that, but the answer that says what actually failed - ownership, with the caller known - is `403`, as the lesson frames it." Mirror in vi.
